text:
### Observed differences

- Participation in six activities flipped in a mirrored way. In the earlier window, A16, A17 and A18 each appeared in about 75 in 100 traces (150 of 200); in the later window each appears in about 25 in 100 (49 of 200). A19, A20 and A21 moved the opposite way, from about 25 in 100 traces (50 of 200) to about 76 in 100 (151 of 200). None of the six activities repeats within a trace in either window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- A15 occurs in every trace in both windows, and its outgoing transitions redistributed: before, about 27 in 100 went to A16, 26 to A18 and 23 to A17, against only about 4–14 in 100 to A19, A20 or A21; in the later window about 22–29 in 100 go to each of A19, A20 and A21, while A16, A17 and A18 each receive only about 8–9 in 100. [DIR001]
- The relations of A15 flip accordingly. Before, A15 co-occurred with A16, A17 and A18 in about 75 in 100 traces, always preceding them; in the later window it co-occurs with each of them in only about 25 in 100 and appears without them in about 76 in 100. With A19, A20 and A21 the picture is inverted: co-occurrence rises from about 25 to about 76 in 100, almost always with A15 first. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- The two sets of three activities behave as mutually exclusive blocks in both windows. A16, A17 and A18 co-occurred with one another in about 75 in 100 traces before (both orders roughly equally, e.g. A16 before A17 in 38 and A17 before A16 in 37) and in about 25 in 100 after, with none of them present in about 76 in 100 later traces; A19, A20 and A21 show the mirror image (co-occurrence about 25 before, about 76 after, again in both orders). No trace contains activities from both sets in either window. [REL007, REL013, REL022, REL023, REL025, REL009, REL014, REL018]
- A25 runs in essentially all traces throughout. Before, it co-occurred with A16, A17 or A18 in about 75 in 100 traces (A16 preceded A25 in 43, with interleaving or repetition in 32) and with A19–A21 in about 25 in 100; in the later window it co-occurs with A19, A20 or A21 in about 76 in 100 (A19 before A25 in 40, interleaved in 36) and with A16–A18 in about 25 in 100. [REL012, REL017, REL021, REL024, REL026, REL027]
- The positional gap between A15 and A20 shortened somewhat: among observed pairs within five steps, a gap of 3 positions fell from about 52 in 100 to about 34 in 100, while a gap of 1 rose from about 16 to about 29. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the route taken after A15 changed: in the later window, execution following A15 passes to the group A19, A20 and A21 — which run together in either order and are typically followed by A25 — in about three quarters of traces, whereas before it passed to the group A16, A17 and A18 in about three quarters of traces, with A25 running in essentially every case in both windows. [DIR001, REL001, REL004, REL022, REL024, OCC001, OCC004]

The routing change is shown directly at A15, whose successor shares moved from roughly 75 in 100 towards A16–A18 to roughly 76 in 100 towards A19–A21, and the participation, direction, relation and lag items all describe the same coherent shift; the swings are large (about 50 in 100 traces, on supports of 150 versus 49 and 50 versus 151), the 35 qualifying items far exceed the roughly half an item expected by chance when screening 106 units, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [DIR001, OCC001, OCC004, REL004, LAG001]

The evidence cannot rule out that the process always offered both routes and only the share of cases taking each changed — a shift in the mix of two pre-existing variants rather than a modified routing rule. In addition, the order within each group is mixed in both windows, so no fixed internal sequence can be asserted, and the finite samples of 200 traces per window cannot fully exclude sampling differences in variant frequencies, although a swing of this size is far beyond what random re-splits typically produce. [REL007, REL022, REL009]
